decisions.mark: states that MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY is the gate, and that it is commented out in the shipped mbedtls_config.h
decisions.detail: QUOTE: With `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` off (the default in `mbedtls_config.h:208`), `include/mbedtls/platform.h:167` makes `mbedtls_calloc` expand straight to `calloc` | WHY: The answer names MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY as the switch and says it is off by default in mbedtls_config.h. But it never says the macro is commented out in the shipped header. It also hedges that "confirm it against the shipped header", so the commented-out claim is not clearly stated.

decisions.mark: concludes that in a DEFAULT build there is no indirection at all — mbedtls_calloc and mbedtls_free are preprocessor macros expanding directly to calloc and free
decisions.detail: QUOTE: With `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` off (the default in `mbedtls_config.h:208`), `include/mbedtls/platform.h:167` makes `mbedtls_calloc` expand straight to `calloc`, and `:166` does the same for `mbedtls_free`. Nothing is indirected. | WHY: The answer states that in the default build the macros expand directly to calloc/free with no indirection.

decisions.mark: distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "**Compile-time.** Enable `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` and define `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO` ... **Run-time.** Enable `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free)`" | WHY: The answer names both the compile-time macro pair and the run-time function-pointer pair, but never says they are mutually exclusive. It also describes the runtime pointers as the default target of the macro path, which implies they work together.

decisions.mark: states that on the macro path mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free does not exist at all — it is neither declared nor compiled, rather than being present and ignored
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says nothing about `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` being absent (undeclared and uncompiled) on the macro path. It describes the function only as the run-time route and says macro-path calls bypass the pointer hop.

decisions.mark: identifies that the pointers' defaults FAIL rather than fall back — an uninitialised calloc returns NULL and an uninitialised free does nothing
decisions.detail: QUOTE: (if that is undefined, platform_calloc_uninit returns NULL) | WHY: The answer says the uninit calloc returns NULL but never states that the uninitialised free does nothing, and it doesn't frame the defaults as failing rather than falling back.

decisions.mark: identifies the buffer allocator (MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C) as the only in-tree user of the runtime setter, installing itself over the pointers from its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Built-in heap allocator. `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init(buf, len)` (`memory_buffer_alloc.c:566`) carves allocations out of a caller-supplied buffer. It calls `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` to point the hooks at its own functions." Also: "the only internal caller is the built-in allocator below" | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator's init function calls the runtime setter to install its own functions, and that it is the only internal caller. It doesn't name MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C, but the allocator and its location are identified.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator installs a MUTEXED pair when MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is on and a plain pair otherwise, chosen at compile time inside its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: With `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`, those are mutex-wrapped variants (`buffer_alloc_calloc_mutexed` / `buffer_alloc_free_mutexed`, lines 541-563). | WHY: The answer says the init function (`memory_buffer_alloc_init`) installs mutex-wrapped calloc/free variants when `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is on. It doesn't say outright that the plain pair is used otherwise, or that the choice is made at compile time, but both are implied by the `#if`-style conditioning.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator itself requires MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, so enabling it alone is not enough to route the library's allocations through it
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer never says the buffer allocator (memory_buffer_alloc) itself requires MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, so enabling that option alone isn't enough to route allocations through it.
